newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse posts $34 million fourth-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse posts $34 million fourth-quarter loss.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Tuesday it lost $34 million in its fourth quarter as restructuring costs continued to take a bite out of earnings.
Westinghouse said its sales grew to $2.5 billion from $1.9 billion a year ago.

The results for the most recent quarter included a one-time charge of $91 million related to the company's restructuring, while the year-earlier period included a charge of $125 million for restructuring and litigation.
The most recent loss, equal to 8 cents a share, compared with a loss of $7 million, or 2 cents a share, a year earlier.

Over the past 16 months, Westinghouse has acquired CBS, Infinity Broadcasting and two country-themed cable television networks as it transforms itself into a broadcasting company. At the same time, Westinghouse has announced the spinoff of its industrial and technology group.

For the year, Westinghouse earned $30 million, or 7 cents a share, on revenue of $8.45 billion. In 1995, the company earned $15 million on revenue of $5.60 billion. Its per share result for 1995 was a loss of 5 cents due to dividends paid on preferred shares.
